system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: At 13:44 UTC, WS-MLOPEZ-01 requested https://raw.githubusercontent.com/harbor-dental-it/tools/main/u.ps1 through the proxy; the GET returned status 200.
At 13:49 UTC, WS-MLOPEZ-01 made an SMB connection to DC-HD-01, with a machine-account network logon recorded on the domain controller.
At 14:12 UTC, WS-MLOPEZ-01 made another SMB connection to DC-HD-01, also associated with a machine-account network logon.
At 14:14 UTC, maria.lopez's medium-integrity cmd.exe process ran netstat -an | findstr LISTENING from Explorer.
At 14:16 UTC, maria.lopez's medium-integrity PowerShell process, launched from Explorer, ran Invoke-WebRequest against packages.nuget.org/api/v2 and exited about 11 seconds later.
The endpoint records show Kerberos and LDAP activity with DC-HD-01 around 13:40 UTC, but those records identify LSASS as the network process and do not establish PowerShell execution.
The GitHub URL appears to use an organization-named repository, but the available records do not establish that the script's contents or execution were approved.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied sensor-coverage metadata reports a winsec and Sysmon collection outage on WS-MLOPEZ-01 from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC, covering the reported 13:40 event and the 13:44 script request. Endpoint process creation, command-line, and related local activity may therefore be missing in that interval.
Proxy and Zeek connection records provide network activity but do not establish which endpoint process initiated the 13:44 request or what the requested script contained.
The available SMB records show connections and authentication but do not identify the accessed share, files, or actions performed.
claims_not_established: Whether PowerShell actually ran at approximately 13:40 UTC, and, if so, its command line, parent process, user context, or outcome.
Whether the u.ps1 script was executed, what its contents were, or whether it was an approved organizational tool.
Whether the SMB connections to DC-HD-01 involved legitimate access or attempted unauthorized activity.
Whether the 14:16 PowerShell request to packages.nuget.org was related to the reported window or the earlier script request.
Whether any data was accessed, changed, or exfiltrated.
additional_evidence_needed: Recover or obtain endpoint process, PowerShell, and security logs for WS-MLOPEZ-01 covering 13:30–14:10 UTC, including backup or EDR telemetry if available.
Retrieve and verify the contents, repository history, and organizational approval status of u.ps1; check whether it was executed on WS-MLOPEZ-01.
Review FILE-HD-01 and DC-HD-01 SMB/share-access logs around 13:49 and 14:12 UTC to determine the resources accessed and actions taken.
Correlate the 14:16 PowerShell activity and packages.nuget.org access with user activity, software-installation records, and any relevant browser or application logs.
